div.p: In the year 1872 Venezuela proposed, and discussed with the legation of the United States of North America at Caracas, a convention by which they might lend their good offices to Venezuela on account of the pecuniary diplomatic reclamations, receiving from this government, in order to distribute among the creditor governments, the product of the part of the receipts applied annually to the amortization of this debt, by means of bases which had not then arrived at perfection.

The undersigned, minister ad interim of exterior relations, executes the order of his government in communicating to the most excellent minister of the United States, with the request that he will deign to notify it to his, that the illustrious American, President of Venezuela, renews the proposal of said convention, with the understanding (en la inteligencia) that there will be delivered not only the sum of 80,000 bolivars, to which the monthly quotas now amount, or 960,000 bolivars per annum, but up to a maximum of 1,040,000 bolivars annually; and that General William A. Pile is authorized to celebrate the convention on the part of the republic ad referendum, to which effect he carries circumstantial and precise instructions, and has knowledge of all the details relative to the fiscal state of the republic. The regulation being made in the terms indicated, it may be clothed with the proper formalities.

The President of the republic cherishes the hope that the most excellent Mr. Baker will vouchsafe to favor the idea and recommend it to the Government of Washington, with his merited influence, since its acceptance will tend to avoid European complications in America, as without doubt the great republic desires, and has manifested various times.
